content:
maria: Heads-up: saw a production case where a tenant lost prefix residency after an eviction + rollback. App observed increased 503s. Looking for a quick sync on safety guarantees and what we should be surfacing in metrics/logs.

oli: ouch. do you have trace ids? can we repro locally or was this only in prod? :thinking_face:

maria: trace: trace-7f3a2d. repro only in prod so far; sequence looked like: eviction started -> storage flush failed -> runtime retried -> tenant ended up demoted but the app kept sending p50-sized requests. we saw double-evict attempts.

vikram: two questions: (1) is eviction atomic with lease state? (2) how do we detect rollback vs normal demote?

oli: currently eviction is a best-effort workflow: acquire lease -> write eviction marker -> async persist -> release. if persist fails we try to rollback markers but there are races w/ handoff. not atomic.

jen: this seems like a correctness hazard. options: make eviction commit idempotent + attach an evict_id and persist before releasing lease, or keep the current flow but add compensating invariants + strong observability. both have perf tradeoffs.

maria: agreed. short term we need better signals so SRE can page before app impact. what metrics would help?

vikram: propose minimal set: 1) counter evict.attempt (tags: tenant, shard, prefix_len) 2) counter evict.commit.success / evict.commit.failure 3) counter evict.rollback (includes reason tag e.g. persist_fail, lease_lost) 4) histogram evict.commit.latency 5) gauge prefix.residency_state with enum tags (hot,cold,handoff-inflight). also trace IDs propagated through RPCs.

oli: +1 for evict.rollback and reason tags. we should also emit eviction_op_id (uuid) on every related log/metric and wire it into the trace. makes debugging across services way easier. :thumbsup:

maria: runtime-side change idea: attach evict_id to lease object and include it in the lease heartbeat. that way a rollback that loses the lease is detectable by comparing last_applied_evict_id.

jen: sketch pseudocode for review:
```
function evict(prefix):
  evict_id = uuid()
  lease = acquire_lease(prefix.tenant)
  write_marker(prefix, evict_id)
  persist_result = persist_marker(prefix, evict_id)
  if !persist_result.ok:
    emit_metric("evict.rollback", {tenant, shard, reason: persist_result.err, evict_id})
    revert_marker(prefix, evict_id)
    release_lease(lease)
    return error
  commit_marker(prefix, evict_id)
  release_lease(lease)
  emit_metric("evict.commit.success", {tenant, shard, evict_id})
```

vikram: couple notes: - revert_marker must be idempotent w/ concurrent handoff; - persist should be strongly-ordered (fsync) or rely on a write-ahead log so we don't lose commits; both increase latency.

jen: for observability: dashboard suggestions: - Eviction health overview: rates + failures by tenant (heatmap) - Evict rollback traces sampled 100% for first 24h after deploy - SLA alert: evict.rollback.rate > 0.1% over 5m for paid tenants -> page P1

oli: question: do we want to differentiate rollback that was deliberate (operator-initiated revert) vs system failure? reason tag should cover it, but ensure operators use a consistent reason enum.

maria: ops-bot: can you link the last incident runbook?

ops-bot: <https://redwood-internal/ops/runbooks/eviction-rollback> (automated) :robot_face:

jen: next steps proposal: 1) add evict_id propagation + eviction.metrics (spike, low-risk) 2) add evict.rollback counter + reason tags (quick) 3) prototype commit-before-release flow in a canary (jen takes) 4) dashboard + 24h high-sample tracing for the canary

maria: timeline? can we have a spike + small PR this week?

jen: I can do the spike today, PR by EOD Fri for the metric bits. will open an RFC if commit-before-release needs more design.

vikram: add tests: simulate persist failure + concurrent handoff, assert no double-evict leaves stale state. we should add a small chaos test to the rack harness.

oli: sounds good. one more: add metric dimension prefix_temperature (hot/cold) so we can correlate rollbacks to hot keys causing contention.

maria: nice. thanks all. i'll file the incident note with trace id and link this thread. :sparkles:

jen: tagging follow-up todo: create spike ticket (#INF-4219), add metrics PR, and post progress in #eng-runtime.

oli: :eyes:

maria: closing the sync for now, ping if you need more traces.
